title: Exceptional coefficient construction: integral scalar mates
statement:
Fix a finite-field datum $D=(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ with $k=\overline{k_0}$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and finite extensions $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation rings $R_E$, uniformizers $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=R_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $k$-morphism; neither $X$ nor $Y$ is assumed separated over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Fix a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow j\overline X\xrightarrow{p_c}Y)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Write $\mathcal C_{T,R_E}$ for the full bounded constructible derived-complete category over the completed coefficient sheaf $\widehat R_{E,T}$, with common finite cohomological and Tor intervals for all derived reductions [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], and $I_{T,R_E}$ for its inclusion in the ordinary derived category. Write $\mathcal R_T$ for the derived reduction system, $\mathcal L_T$ for total derived inverse limit, and $\mathsf N_T$ for normalized strict coefficient systems whose every level $M_n$ lies in the bounded constructible finite-Tor category $D^b_{ctf}(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], with those same common bounds: each transition-adjoint $A_{E,n}\otimes^L_{A_{E,m}}M_m\to M_n$ is an isomorphism [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Take $F_R,G_R$ to be the reduction/limit transport of the ordinary etale proper/open system adjunction and its specified ambient realization, with $F_R$ identified with the prescribed integral compact support [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. For a finite extension $E\to L$ let $e$ be its ramification index, so $R_L/\varpi_E^nR_L=A_{L,en}$. The system restriction to indices $en$ is an equivalence on normalized systems, whose inverse has level $m$ equal to $A_{L,m}\otimes^L_{A_{L,en}}M_n$ for the least $n$ with $en\ge m$, with the normalization transition maps. It carries the finite-free system scalar comparisons to the full $L$-tower.

For integral reduction $R_E\to A_{E,n}$ choose the literal restriction of ordinary derived extension, with equality realization. For completed extension $R_E\to R_L$ choose the published strict-tower functor $T_{L/E}$ [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. It preserves the same common Tor interval and is realized in the ambient category by $\theta=\chi_{L/E}^{-1}$, where $\chi_{L/E}$ is the canonical comparison from ordinary derived extension to strict-tower scalar extension. For these generators, and every identity or composite of their actual coefficient-sheaf maps and finite quotient/ramified maps, there are invertible shift-compatible $q:T_YF_s\cong F_tT_X$ and $b:T_XG_s\cong G_tT_Y$ satisfying
$$\epsilon_{t,T_YL}\circ F_t(b_L)\circ q_{G_sL}=T_Y(\epsilon_{s,L}).$$
Their left realizations are exactly the ambient proper scalar mate followed by the open tensor map. Integral reduction agrees with actual system evaluation, including its units and counits; completed extension agrees with the finite-free system maps under $\chi$ and the proper/open realization. All identities hold before total limit and retain the canonical termwise and Roos-cone shifts.

For an allowed composite choose the scalar functor for its actual ring-sheaf map. There are scalar identity and composition isomorphisms, whose realized maps are respectively $x\otimes r\mapsto rx$ and $(x\otimes s)\otimes t\mapsto x\otimes b(s)t$ on flat models. Under these balanced tensor identifications the composite $q$ is the proper/open mate for the composite map, and the composite $b$ satisfies the same counit equation. The construction thus supplies the normalized scalar data for every allowed witness, without identifying the indices $en$ and $n$.

source.place: Propositions 2.23, 2.29, 3.16; Section 5, especially Lemma 5.22 and Proposition 5.24; blueprint exceptional inverse-image construction. Specific obligation: returned construction steps 13–16, preserved verbatim in the delivery report.

proof.text: Use the given reduction/limit transport with the actual unit and counit specified by integral reconstruction. For $a:R_E\to A_{E,n}$ let $T_{a,T}$ be the literal restriction of ordinary derived tensor. Its output is the defining reduction of an integral finite-Tor object. The evaluation comparisons identify $T_{a,Y}F_R$ with $F_{A_{E,n}}T_{a,X}$ and $T_{a,X}G_R$ with $G_{A_{E,n}}T_{a,Y}$, with their units and counits. Call these maps $q_a,b_a$. The system-transport theorem gives these as transported system adjunction maps, so the evaluated counit equation is precisely $\epsilon_tF_t(b_a)q_{a,G_R}=T_{a,Y}\epsilon_R$. The reduction/limit counit is the scalar adjunct of the actual limit projection, rather than an unspecified identification of objects. The proper/open realization intertwines these units, counits and tensor maps; hence the left realization of $q_a$ is the ambient proper scalar mate followed by the open tensor map.

source.place: Construction 5.15, Lemmas 5.16 and 5.22, Proposition 5.26; integral reduction with the specified reconstruction counit.

proof.text: Put $B_m=A_{L,m}$ and $r(n)=en$. Apply the subsequence adjunction $L_r\dashv U_r$ to strict systems, with $t(m)=\min\{n:en\ge m\}$. Its evaluation is $e_mL_rN=B_m\otimes^L_{B_{et(m)}}N_{t(m)}$ with the stated selected-level transitions. On a normalized $M$, the counit $L_rU_rM\to M$ evaluates to the normalization isomorphism $B_m\otimes^L_{B_{et(m)}}M_{et(m)}\to M_m$. On a selected system $N$, $t(en)=n$, so the unit $N\to U_rL_rN$ evaluates to the tensor unitor. Joint conservativity proves these are isomorphisms. The transition formula shows $L_rN$ is normalized whenever $N$ is; testing its $m$th tensor with a $B_m$-module is the same test on $N_{t(m)}$, so the common Tor interval is preserved. Its unit test gives the same common cohomological interval, and its finite coefficients preserve constructibility by the finite scalar lemma. Thus these adjunction maps restrict to inverse equivalences on the normalized categories in the statement. R9 realizes this recovery argument by systemSelectedAdjunctionIsos (fully proved unit and normalized counit), systemSelectedNormalization, restrictionBounds (fully proved selection and isomorphism transport), and ramifiedSystemRecoveryBounds. Assemble restricts and recovers using the same witnesses a,b,c,d and their original order inequalities. The recovery-bounds statement is the remaining independent finite-quotient bound step.

source.place: Construction 4.1; derived subsequence left extension, applied to r(n)=en. The equivalence assertion is the displayed unit/counit calculation.

proof.text: At selected levels $R_L/\varpi_E^nR_L=A_{L,en}$ use the finite-free scalar comparison of the ordinary etale system adjunction. The left map is the actual system coefficient projection $q$, and the right map is the counit-normalized system transpose $b$; both are invertible and include every transition. The cofinal-mate theorem identifies the right adjoint restricted from the full $L$-tower with this selected-level right adjoint, preserving counits. Use the equivalence of Step 2 to recover the full tower; no level $en$ is identified with level $n$. Transport along the etale/pro-etale system equivalence, with its actual units and counits. Tensor/pullback and proper/open realization give the same scalar arrows there: finite-free coefficient extension is tensor by the coefficient system, so it is among the tensor expressions of the realization theorem. This produces an invertible system $q,b$ on the normalized pro-etale inputs, and its counit equation holds as a derived-system equation before any total limit.

source.place: Construction 4.1, Construction 5.15 and Lemma 5.22; finite-free extension followed by the cofinal-mate comparison.

proof.text: For completed extension choose exactly the published strict-tower functor $T_{L/E}$. The canonical $\chi_{L/E}:S_{L/E}\to I_LT_{L/E}$ is a natural isomorphism on derived-complete inputs by the finite-free completed-scalar comparison, where $S_{L/E}$ is ordinary derived extension after inclusion. Constructibility is preserved by the integral scalar-extension theorem. The adic Tor-bound theorem gives, at arbitrary level $m$ and any $n$ with $en\ge m$, the reduction $K_n\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}A_{L,m}$ and the same interval $[a,b]$. These facts verify that this chosen functor restricts to the required categories. Set $\theta=\chi^{-1}$; the completed-scalar normalization is then the specified one, without changing the scalar functor.

source.place: Section 5, finite-free integral extension; completed coefficients as in Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 6.8.2(1) and the explicitly cited completed-scalar theorem.

proof.text: Apply the reconstruction equivalences to the actual system transformations of Step 3. Use their units and counits to identify the resulting integral operations with the given $F_R,G_R$, and identify their scalar functors with the choice in Step 4 as follows. For integral $K$ with flat-term K-flat representative, $\chi$ gives $T_{L/E}K\cong K\otimes^L_{\widehat R_E}\widehat R_L$, which is derived complete and lies in the integral category, so the reconstruction unit identifies it with $\mathcal L_L\mathcal R_L$ of itself. Balanced associativity identifies $U_r\mathcal R_L(K\otimes^L\widehat R_L)$ with the selected-level finite-free extension $(K_n\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}A_{L,en})_n$ of $\mathcal R_EK$, as systems, since that comparison is natural in the composable ring maps and so respects transitions; the counit of $L_r\dashv U_r$ then identifies $\mathcal R_L(K\otimes^L\widehat R_L)$ with $L_r$ of it, the Step 2 recovery of the full tower. Conjugating the system counit identity by these isomorphisms gives $\epsilon_{t,T_YL}F_t(b_L)q_{G_sL}=T_Y(\epsilon_{s,L})$; functors and conjugation preserve composition. Each comparison is invertible because its system comparison and every conjugating map are invertible. For the left realization apply $c_V$ to the tensor-by-coefficients and proper/open expressions: its generator-map clause identifies the tensor/pullback map and proper counit with the corresponding integral maps. The open map is the unique open-adjunction transpose of the scalar extension of the open unit. Consequently the realized $q$ is exactly the ambient proper scalar mate followed by that open tensor map, with the prescribed $\chi$ and proper/open realization. This proves equality of these normalized integral maps through the coherent system construction, rather than through faithfulness of finite evaluations.

source.place: Lemma 5.22 and Proposition 5.26; agent assembly through the named reconstruction and proper/open generator-map realizations.

proof.text: Give scalar extension its canonical cochain shift. Proper mates are made from shift-compatible derived units/counits and tensor/pullback maps; the open tensor map is degreewise the same balanced tensor map. The realization shift theorem applies to these same bounded normalized expressions and their generator maps, and to Steps 1 and 5. For $\chi$ the completed-scalar chain-shift theorem gives the product shift on the first cone coordinate and $(-1)^r$ times it on the second coordinate for shift $r$; the zero second component of the quotient comparison stays zero. Thus $\theta=\chi^{-1}$ also preserves these canonical Roos-cone shifts. Right-adjoint shift structures are the unique ones compatible with unit and counit. Taking the transpose of a shifted left comparison therefore gives the shifted $b$, by its defining counit equation and injectivity of adjunction. All generator $q,b$ are shift-compatible for these specified shifts.

source.place: Agent shift verification for the canonical system, termwise and Roos-cone models; blueprint adic-stage construction.

proof.text: For each allowed actual coefficient-sheaf map choose the scalar functor according to its target: literal ambient restriction at a finite target, the published completed extension at an integral target. Finite generators use the finite scalar lemma; integral generators use Steps 1–6. Balanced derived associativity gives $(S_bS_a)\cong S_{ba}$, represented by $(x\otimes s)\otimes t\mapsto x\otimes b(s)t$, and scalar units give $S_{\mathrm{id}}\cong\mathrm{id}$, represented by $x\otimes r\mapsto rx$. Conjugate these ambient maps through the scalar realizations $\theta$ and lift through the full inclusions. Fullness supplies the maps, faithfulness gives their naturality and the identities for their inverses. This constructs the scalar identity and composition isomorphisms with exactly the asserted ambient realizations, including mixed finite-quotient/completed-extension composites.

source.place: Agent assembly from Stacks Tags 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition) and 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat); scalar units and associators.

proof.text: For composable allowed maps $a:s\to t$, $c:t\to u$, write $V=T_c$, $T=T_a$ and suppress the balanced scalar associators. Define $q_{ca}=(q_cT_X)\circ V_Y(q_a)$ and $b_{ca}=(b_cT_Y)\circ V_X(b_a)$. For the proper factor, the coefficient-projection cocycle identifies this pasted $q$ with the canonical proper scalar mate for the composite coefficient map; its identity clause gives the proper unitor. For the open factor, restrict both composites to the open. The open-unit normalization identifies both with the same balanced tensor associator; injectivity of the open-adjunction bijection gives equality before restriction. Hence the pasted proper/open $q$ is the specified one for the actual composite, including identities. The cocycle and open normalization are statements on ringed diagram sites, so this conclusion holds for system maps before total limit and is carried to the integral realization by its generator-map clause.

source.place: Stacks Tag 0E47 (remark-compose-base-change-horizontal), and the open-unit comparison on ringed diagram sites.

proof.text:
Check the right composite explicitly. With the notation of Step 8 and composition read right to left, its counit composite is
$$\epsilon_u F_u(b_cT_Y)F_uV_X(b_a)q_{c,T_XG_s}V_Y(q_{a,G_s}).$$
Naturality of $q_c$ moves $F_uV_X(b_a)$ past $q_c$, replacing their product by $q_{c,G_tT_Y}V_YF_t(b_a)$. The equation for $c$ changes the first three factors into $V_Y(\epsilon_tF_t(b_a))$; the equation for $a$ then gives $V_YT_Y(\epsilon_s)$. Reinsert the scalar associators of Step 7 to obtain exactly the required composite counit equation. This also proves that $b_{ca}$ is the counit-normalized transpose of $q_{ca}^{-1}$, by the adjunction bijection. For identities the same equation is the triangle identity under the multiplication unitor.

source.place: Elementary substitution of the two counit equations already established in Steps 1 and 5, and naturality of q; no additional lemma.

proof.text: Induct on an allowed witness, using the generator comparisons, the identity unitors and the composite construction of Steps 7–9. Every resulting $q,b$ is invertible as a composite of isomorphisms. The balanced associators preserve shifts, and composition, inversion and whiskering preserve shift-compatible transformations, so these properties hold for every witness. The proper/open cocycle fixes the realized left map for its actual coefficient map; Step 9 fixes the right map by the counit equation. At each stage use actual system transformations and only then their total-limit images. This proves every asserted normalization and preserves the canonical termwise and cone shifts.

source.place: Induction on identity/composite coefficient witnesses, using the preceding generator equations and canonical balanced tensor identifications.

proof.text: For the main exceptionalIntegralScalarMates conclusion, use the already stated core theorem for the scalar, reduction and system data. For each e>0 and source index n, the product e(n+1) is positive, so write it as m+1. Transport finiteChange and Allowed.ramified along this equality to construct RamifiedMap with source n. Its actual-map equality is heterogeneous reflexivity, and its source-index equality is reflexivity. Pair this explicit witness with the core data. The original ten-step plan remains above for the core construction and the separate ramifiedRecovery theorem, which are still open.

proof_origin.place: Explicit assembly of Zheng Construction 4.1, Construction 5.15, Lemmas 5.16 and 5.22 and Proposition 5.26 through the cited existing derived-system, reconstruction and normalized realization statements. The precise shift and ambient-map assertions use the separately stated DAG tools, not an unquoted claim of Zheng. K3: the main theorem now applies the existing core theorem and proves the independent explicit ramified-index witness. The original plan is retained for the remaining core and ramifiedRecovery holes. R9: ramifiedRecovery is assembled from normalization preservation, proven actual adjunction isomorphisms, proven restriction bounds, and the separate finite-quotient recovery-bounds step.
